key_insight: Matrix-free fast diagonalization and tailored preconditioners accelerate high-order finite element elliptic solves on distributed GPUs by reducing both iteration counts and per-iteration cost.
engineering_relevance: Faster elliptic solves can reduce computational bottlenecks in large-scale engineering simulations using high-order finite elements.
method: Distributed exact fast-diagonalization solver for supported tensor-product meshes and coefficient structures.
Hybrid Schwarz with exact FD cell inverses and p-multigrid with fused hanging-node constraint handling.
FP32 acceleration within FP64 conjugate gradients, adaptive coarse-level distribution, and CUDA/HIP/SYCL support.
evidence_signal: Tests span uniform, graded and octree meshes across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs: direct FD is 100–1,000× faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes, while HS-FD converges in 11 iterations across 8–1,024 MI250X graphics compute dies for an octree generalized Poisson problem.
watch_item: Exact direct FD requires supported tensor-product structure and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction; FP32 acceleration also depends on cell shapes and coefficients.
paper_title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for higher-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
